claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled 'SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi' exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ and covers the engine mechanics behind SST's migration to Pulumi.
AWS CDK tied infrastructure to AWS, and multi-cloud with CDK was nearly impossible.
AWS CDK allowed developers to define infrastructure using TypeScript or Python.
AWS CDK supports only TypeScript and Python.
Once Ion is stable, it will be released as SST v3; Ion is the code name for SST's new engine deploying with Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation.
SST uses Pulumi for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
Pulumi supports defining infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C# and deploying to AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and on-premises.
AWS CDK secrets management is limited to AWS Secrets Manager only.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account or Pulumi Cloud; the engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps its state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account.
Nitric and Defang run application deployments through the Pulumi engine.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, supporting AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST apps define infrastructure in a single sst.config.ts file.
Through 2023 SST's provisioning layer was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation.
In late 2023 the SST team began a rewrite code-named Ion, which shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN).'
SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says that on sst deploy, resources call an embedded Pulumi engine that calls the bridged Terraform provider, which makes AWS SDK calls.
SST docs 'What is SST' say: 'SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi.'
Gautier Blandin's article 'Terraform, Pulumi, SST: a tradeoff analysis' says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says: 'You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now.'
SST's platform/package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds and others, and the Pulumiverse Vercel provider.
The Pulumi engine diffs desired vs actual state, builds a dependency graph, and orders operations; Terraform-bridged providers translate resources into cloud API calls.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API allows embedding Pulumi programs inside other tools, and the provider bridge lets any Pulumi user consume Terraform providers directly.
Nitric's docs state 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments', with official Nitric providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed as part of the same SST app.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The sst npm package gets roughly 796,000 downloads per week (796,291 for September 5-11, 2026).
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode has a larger GitHub following than SST.
SST doesn't invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
The SST repository is anomalyco/sst (formerly sst/sst).
